doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing society dance music with Willie Lewis at Chez Florence
summary: The Lewis band played show tunes and melody for a jet-set crowd, with few Carter arrangements.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What sort of music did you find that you were playing with Willie Lewis, his band?

Well, Willie Lewis was a clarinetist and saxophonist who had gone to Europe with the Sam Wooding Orchestra. So, you know, it was sort of as a jazz orchestra, but we played mostly society music, because we played in a club called the Chez Florence and mostly

people who would today be considered . . . the clientele, at least, were people who today would be considered members of the jet set, you know. I guess those are the people we were playing for. We played for dancing. Primarily, it was a dance band, and you played a lot of melody, you know, with very little improvisation. You know, they played all the show tunes and things like that.
You eventually began to contribute some arrangements to Willie Lewis.
But those were anything but—quote, unquote—“society music.”
How did you get away with . . . did you sneak those in, or were those . . .
Well, you know, there were very few of those, really, in what we played. I mean, I wrote very few of those, and as you’re saying, we might have snuck them in, you know.
Was it possible they were mostly for recording, because they were recorded.
I don’t remember. No, I don’t remember.
You don’t remember if they were part of the regular repertoire of the orchestra.
